_about: The convoy war by cause (audit #5; the design director's ruling of 23 November 2026 07:26Z on the form naval-battles/convoy-r2/form.md). Read only in a grand campaign opened with Units decide (src/campaign/units.ts); off, nothing here is read. One rule for every navy and both sides: the kit a navy holds and the work its ships are given set each figure, never the nation or the month. Every size is OEG Report 51's (naval-battles/wolfpack-r2/history.md, where each is marked).
_cover: OEG T7: ships torpedoed a day were 0.60 with air cover against 1.75 without. The raiders in a sea sink at this share of their rate over the waters that aircraft carrying anti-submarine kit reach. Without that kit, aircraft only force boats down; that figure is not laid, so no cut is given for it.
_asv: Aircraft carry anti-submarine kit when their navy (or its senior partner) holds depth charges for aircraft (the tree's 'sonar') and this research: sea-search radar, which also fits its escorts. (The form's first reading, the radar branch's second design, hung the kit on Fighter control, an air-defence row Britain's staff took only in January 1945.)
_find: OEG T2: 41-43% of convoys were attacked. The share of the boats raiding a convoy route's seas that find a convoy and attack it in a month; each is one incident with the convoy's escort.
_incident: OEG 51 ch. 11 Table 10 (F; historian/escort-kill-denominator-1124.md): US escorts' attacks in the Atlantic and Mediterranean, the share of incidents assessed sunk. An incident is a U-boat the escorts actually attacked, all attacks on it in one engagement counted once, before or after it fired. Two columns, independent and coordinated (OEG defines neither beyond its title): the game lays coordinated on a support group (destroyers on hunting duty in that sea) and independent on the convoy's close escort (destroyers bound to its route) (D). With the escorts' losses form laid (_escorts, the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 17:58Z, Q2 (a)), an incident is coordinated with the chance spare / (spare + on stations), the spare ships the support groups in the route's seas, shared over the route's convoys at sea at once (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 22:24Z, 3 (b)), and the escorts with each convoy beyond the close screen's stations, and independent otherwise, the escorts on the stations; each ship at its own navy's column and kit steps. The record's two rows split by date, Jan 1943-Feb 1944 (0.05, 0.17: the 0.17 is 3 kills in 18, about 4-41% at 95%, D) and Mar 1944-May 1945 (0.12, 0.55: 21 in 38 for the 0.55); the game credits the step between them to kit, escort-group training and coordinated hunting together (D), laid on ahead-throwing weapons with escort-group training, never the date. With the escorts' losses form unread (escorts null), read on the count's incidents, the boats that fired: the interim of the radar ruling's Q3 (a), which under-counts where radar frustrates (the boats found and driven off were the ones attacked). Laid, as shipped, the incidents are set from the boats that try (the design director, 24 November 2026 16:44Z, ruled at 17:58Z): those the screen frustrates and those it finds after they fire (_escorts, Q1 (a)). atw: ahead-throwing weapons alone, without escort-group training, multiply the depth-charge rate by this (OEG T9: Hedgehog 7.5% against depth charges 4.0% per attack in its first half-year at sea, H2 1943; historian/convoy-figures-for-r2-1123.md). The weapon's later rise (2.6-4.7 times in 1944) is crews learning it, a cause not yet laid, never the month.
_radar: Radar on escorts: what sea-search radar adds to a ship's guard and hunting weight. Not laid (the historian's figure from OEG 10.1.2 and the HF/DF record): 0 until it is read.
_seaLoss: The tree's flat cuts to convoy losses that stay: the convoy system that comes with 'sonar'. Escort groups act through their incidents instead, and no nation's own trait (Britain's signals) is read.
_station: The share of a month a raiding fleet's boats are on station in the sea they raid (the design director's one-pass ruling of 24 November 2026 13:23Z, Q3(a)(i), and the days of 13:31Z; naval-battles/convoy-r2/one-pass-form.md). A cause, not a scale: a patrol's days on station ('patrol') over its whole cycle, which adds the passage out from the fleet's port and back ('passage' days for each sea crossed by the sea graph, through the straits open to it) and the refit in port before the next patrol ('refit'). Share = patrol / (patrol + 2 x passage x seas + refit). It acts wherever boats raiding are counted: the raid strength that sinks tons and the incidents with the convoys' escorts. By class: 'ss' alone has rows; a class without rows is on station all month. The days are laid, never the shares (historian/convoy-build-reads-1124.md): patrol 20, a Biscay boat's days on station of about 40 out (D from L: U-96's 11 patrols averaged 38.6 days out; McCue, NDU 1990); refit 40, its days in port before the next (D from L: U-96's 38.2); passage 5, fitted so the Bay of Biscay to the North Atlantic, two seas on the chart, is McCue's 10 days each way ('20 or more days on the trip to port and back', D). German and Norwegian ports take the same days a sea. Checks, not figures: about 0.25 of boats in commission on station, 0.5 of boats at sea (D), and the record's third (about 104 boats at sea of 240-300 in 1943). Tankers at sea are a cause not yet laid. 'raid': a boat's raid weight while on station in the lanes' form (navy.json classes.ss.raid is 1, a boat there all month), refit once at OEG T2's window so the window keeps its tons with the share: 3.5 (D, the six-war reading of 24 November, naval-battles/convoy-r2/onepass-reading-1124.md; it comes to 1 / 0.286, the window's own share). The lanes' ocean term could not carry it (it would have to be -328). Where the tons are counted from the convoys' side (count.sink below; the tons ruling of 24 November 14:04Z) the boats on station that find and attack carry the share, so the convoys' side counts a boat on station at 1. The 3.5 stays wherever the lanes' form still counts boats: the oil and supply lanes (laneLoss, the ruling's Q4), the escorts' destroyers lost to the boats, and a route whose sinking figure is unread. Null: a weight of 1. 'dd': the escorts' cycle on a convoy route, read only by the firing share below (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 16:58Z, Q1 (d) of naval-battles/convoy-r2/screen-cycle-form.md; historian/escort-screen-cycle-1124.md). The Mid-Ocean Escort Force's 33 days from February 1942 (L): 19 with a convoy (9.5 with a westbound, 9.5 with an eastbound), 6 turnaround at the western end and 8 at the eastern ('refit'), and about a third of strength out of service at any time ('unavailable', L), so 19 / 33 x (1 - 0.333) = 0.38 of the escorts bound to a route are at sea with a convoy at once (D). Boiler cleaning was not found and is not laid. 'crossing': a convoy's days in the escorts' care, 9.5 (L). The convoys at sea at once are the convoys sailed a month (both ways) x the crossing / 30 days (D: the game's month), and the escorts a convoy are the escorts at sea with the convoys over them. One row for every navy's escorts. A null: escorts bound to the route over convoys sailed a month, as first built.
_count: The convoy-side count (one-pass ruling Q1(a), Q2(a), Q4, and the reading ruling of 24 November 13:50Z): a route's convoys attacked a month = convoys sailed x the share attacked. attacked 0.42 and sighted 0.68: OEG ch. 10 Table 2, northern routes, Oct 1942 to May 1943, 80 convoys (F; historian/convoy-reads-1124.md); a contact is a convoy sighted. The share attacked is 1 - exp(-phi x F x B), B the boats on station on the route's seas (station above), F finding from kit (none laid: 1), one phi for every route, fitted so the share is 0.42 at boatsT2. boatsT2 40: the boats at sea in the northwest Atlantic over T2's window, 22 to 60 (D from F, the middle). perAttack 2: boats a convoy attacked (F, OEG's own estimate). Convoys sailed a month = ways x the route's tons / (ships a convoy x GRT a ship). ways 2: T2's 0.42 is over its convoys both ways, so the count takes the return sailings as well as the loaded ones (D, the ruling of 13:50Z: about 10.4 a month on the Atlantic route). The incidents with the escort are counted from the boats' side, at T2's own rate: t2 80 convoys over 8 months (F, OEG T2's window) x 0.42 x 2 boats / 40 on station = 0.21 a boat on station a month (D). The pack, the boats a convoy attacked, follows from the two (incidents / attacked), and the card shows it. With the escorts' losses form laid (_escorts, the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 17:58Z, Q1 (a)), the 0.21 stays the pack's source only, the boats that fired at T2: the escort meets the boats that try by cause instead, for the boats raiding a route, in that build and never before. ships: atlantic 44 (D from L, historian/convoy-size-1124.md); libya 2 (D from L: Bragadin's 883 escorted convoys, the usual operation 2 ships, O'Hara; 1 to 7). grt: atlantic 5,200 (D: every pair read gives 4,400-5,800; ruling 241 Q8); libya 3,800 (D from L: 342 Axis freighters lost, 1,299,777 tons). historian/convoy-build-reads-1124.md. sink (k): the tons ruling (naval-battles/convoy-r2/tons-form.md): a convoy the boats attack loses its ships x P / (P + k x E), P the pack's raid strength (the pack x a boat's raid strength on station, its kit, fit and the air over it), E the convoy's share of the route's escort worth (G / convoys sailed; with the escorts' losses form laid, the escorts on the close screen's stations, and k sinkOnStations, below); tons = convoys attacked x ships sunk x GRT, both ways, and the share of cargo lost is the share of ships sunk. k is refit once at OEG T2's window so that 2 boats sink 3.75 ships a convoy attacked (D: T2's 80 convoys, 125.6 ships sunk over 33.5 convoys attacked; SC/ONS 4.4, HX/ONF 3.2): 0.137 (D, six AI wars Oct 1942 to May 1943, 48 months: a boat's raid strength on station 0.298, a convoy's escort worth 46.5; the months' median 0.136). Never fitted to a battle; the battle table (wolfpack-r2/history.md, P) is a check only. sinkOnStations (k on the stations): the escorts' losses form's Q5, 'price once' (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 17:58Z, from his ruling of 16:58Z), solved as he ruled at 22:24Z, 1 (b). With the escorts beyond the close screen's stations hunting, E is the escorts on the stations with the convoy (a count of ships: the lesser of the escorts with the convoy and the stations, firing.screen), and k is solved once on it at the tons ruling's own record point, on the record's own E there: 2 boats sink 3.75 of the convoy's 44 ships a convoy attacked at OEG T2's window. P is the tons ruling's own: 2 boats x 0.298, a boat's raid strength on station at the window in its six AI wars, 0.596. E is the record's escorts a convoy at T2, about 6.5 (F, OEG ch. 10 Table 5, as firing.rT2 reads them), all of them on stations, for the 44-ship convoy has 10.19. k = P x (ships / sunk - 1) / E = 0.596 x (44 / 3.75 - 1) / 6.5 = 0.596 x 10.733 / 6.5 = 0.984 (D). It is solved once at the record point, record against record, never fitted to the game's tons or to a battle. The game's E on the stations at T2 is higher than the record's: the game has about 35 escorts with each convoy there (33 to 37 in six AI wars, D), so every station of the 44-ship convoy is filled in every month of the six wars, and E is the stations, 6 + (44 / 3.5) / 3 = 10.19 (firing.screen). That is a named fault: the game has too few convoys at sea at once (about 3.3 on the Atlantic route, D; the record's by year are asked of the historian), so too many escorts with each convoy. On the game's full stations 2 boats sink 2.47 ships, not 3.75, and the game's packs at T2 (P about 0.75) meet a contest of about 3.05 ships a convoy attacked, under the boat ceiling's about 3.15 and under T2's 3.2 to 4.4 (D). So the 1943 Atlantic tons fall about 8.0% (3.7% to 13.6%) against k unread, in six AI wars with the support groups shared (D; naval-battles/convoy-r2/escort-losses-reading-2-1124.md). E on the stations x k sets the tons in about 57% of 1942's attacked months and 88% of 1943's, so Q5 prices from 1942. That fall is the named fault's honest effect, shown and never tuned. Solved on the game's 10.19 instead, k would be 0.628 (0.596 x 10.733 / 10.19); that was refused, for it would bake the fault into the constant and need a second refit once the convoy count is mended, against Q5's 'once'. Where the form is laid, 0.984 replaces the tons ruling's 0.137, which was solved on the game's escort worth a convoy there, 46.5, with the same inflation (0.596 x 10.733 / 46.5 = 0.1376); 0.137 stands where the form is unread. Read only where the form is laid; null there, or the form unread: E and k as the tons ruling set them. The month's swing and a fought night act on the ships sunk a convoy attacked, never past its ships (Q3(a)). A surface raider or a fortress astride the route keeps the lanes' form beside it, its tons of the loaded sailings as before; the two shares together at most the lanes' cap (0.95). Null: the boats keep the lanes' form. A route whose count is not laid (a null) keeps the per-boat share above ('find').
_ceiling: The boat ceiling (the design director's rulings of 24 November 2026 14:46Z, corrected 14:49Z, and 16:27Z and 16:31Z on naval-battles/convoy-r2/ceiling-reading-1124.md): the ships one boat sinks in one convoy battle at most on an average night = its torpedoes usable that battle x the share that hit x the ships a hit sinks; a convoy attacked loses at most the pack x that, the pack at least one boat (a convoy attacked has one on it; the count's pack falls under one on Libya, builder's choice of the review). The month's swing and a fought night act around it (mean 1, ruling 241), never past the convoy's ships. inside 12: the torpedoes a VIIC or a IXC carries inside its hull (L, historian/naval-reads-3-1124.md sections 2 and 5: VIIC 5 in the tubes, 6 bow reloads, 1 aft; IXC 6 in the tubes, 6 inside). outside 2: those carried outside the hull in pressure-tight canisters, which a crew can bring inside only in a calm sea and with time on the surface (L). The game has no sea state; the calm sea is read from the sky: with weather, all of them under a clear sky and none under cloud or a closed sky (the builder's reading of 'calm sea (weather)'); with no weather, the share the weather table expects that month, its chance of a clear sky over the sea's zone, and one of two where the table has no sky for the sea (the design director's 16:27Z ruling: the expected value, neither all calm nor all rough). The game builds one boat design; 2 is the VIIC's (L), the type of most boats (M), laid for every boat until a boat design row sets its own (16:27Z); a IXC carried 10. hit 0.45: the share of torpedoes fired that hit, one figure for every boat that fires, in every year (the design director's 16:31Z ruling; D from F: about 4 ships sunk a boat at sea a month, July 1940 to March 1941, OEG 51 chapters 2-3, at 1.4-1.75 hits a ship sunk from about 14 torpedoes; historian/convoy-gap-1940-41-1124.md). The escort's radar acts before a boat fires, not on its hits (historian/torpedo-hits-radar-1124.md: about 70% of attempted attacks frustrated late in 1942, yet about two ships torpedoed in each attack that succeeded, F); how it does is the firing share (_firing, the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 16:35Z), and it is never counted on the hit share. The escort finding a boat after it fires (_escorts, his ruling of 17:58Z) sets the incidents and the kills, never the hits. sinkHit 0.57: the ships sunk for every hit, overkill and ships hit that survived counted, since the ceiling multiplies every hit: 289 ships sunk for 507 or more hits (Hezlet ch. 33, British and Allied submarines against Axis merchant ships, 1941-45, L; D; the design director's 16:27Z correction of 0.7, which is the chance a single hit sinks). So, with the whole load into one convoy (the load form unread), a boat that fires sinks at most 12 x 0.45 x 0.57 = 3.1 ships a convoy battle (D), and 14 x 0.45 x 0.57 = 3.6 in a calm sea. With the load form laid (below, and _load), it fires salvos of its 5 ready tubes, one approach and a further one the next night as seldom as its causes allow: 5 x 0.45 x 0.57 = 1.28 a salvo, about 1.33-1.41 a firing boat in the six wars (load-reading-1124.md); the checks below then read the record's per-boat figures (about 2.3 hits a firing boat in 1941 and 2.7 at T2), and the design director's 2-4 a boat a battle stands for the whole load. The record's checks, never fitted: about 1.0 ship sunk a boat a battle, 0.7-1.8 by convoy size (D from OEG T3, F; its row pairs U; wolfpack-r2/history.md), about 2 ships torpedoed in each attack that succeeded (OEG 5.2.1, F), the design director's 2-4 a boat a battle (14:46Z; the historian's 14:50Z read gives 1-3) and the best single boat's 7 (U-100, U-515, L) the tail, against the most a month's swing books, 1.2 x 3.6. Null in inside, hit or sinkHit: no ceiling, the tons ruling as before. tubes 5 (the load form, 17:37Z): the ready tubes a boat fires in one approach, 4 bow and 1 stern for a VIIC (L, historian/naval-reads-3-1124.md; F, the war diaries: all ready tubes each approach, both eras), the boat type's kit; the game builds one boat design, so 5 for every boat until a boat design row sets its own. With the load form laid (load), a boat that fires puts salvos of its tubes into a convoy, not its whole load, and the load becomes a cap for its patrol. hit 0.45 stays as the share of torpedoes fired in a convoy approach that hit (the design director's 17:37Z ruling: D on its own evidence; 5 x 0.45 is about 2.2 hits an approach, against 2.3 hits a boat a convoy in 1941 and 2.7 at T2; the war diaries' 0.6 claims are an upper check; the boat-month yield, about 4 ships a boat at sea a month in July 1940 to March 1941, is a check on the whole chain).
_firing: The escort's radar before a boat fires (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 16:35Z on naval-battles/convoy-r2/radar-firing-form.md, (a) on all three; historian/torpedo-hits-radar-1124.md). Radar worked mostly before a boat fired, not on its hits: late in 1942 'about 70 per cent of the attempted attacks were frustrated by the escorts', yet 'about two ships were torpedoed in each successful attack' (OEG 51 section 5.2.1, F). The count's pack is the boats that fired (OEG's 'U-boats attacking each contact', measured at T2 against escorts with radar), so the boats that try are the pack / t2, and those that fire are the tries x 1 / (1 + c x r): r the radar-fitted escorts a convoy (the route's escort vessels whose navy has sea-search radar, at their share on the route, over the convoys sailed a month) for each boat trying, c = (1/t2 - 1) / rT2. 1 with no radar-fitted escort (D: 1940's about 4 ships a boat at sea a month at 0.45 a torpedo). Applied once, on the pack that the contest and the ceiling both read; with the escorts' losses form unread the escort's kills keep the count's incidents (Q3 (a)), and laid they read this same contest (_escorts, the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 17:58Z). t2 0.3: the share that fired at T2 (D from F, 70% frustrated). rT2 1: T2's ratio, the record's, never the game's (the design director: the game has about 3 times the record's boats there, a gap the work-up pipeline answers): about 6.5 escorts a convoy (F, OEG ch. 10 Table 5), nearly all with radar (M), over about 6.7 boats trying (2 / 0.3, D); so c = 7/3 (D). The check, never fitted: HX 229/SC 122, March 1943, boats about 2:1 over the escorts, r about 0.5, a share of about 0.46; 21-22 ships lost (L). Null in either: every boat counted fires, as before. The radar-fitted escorts a convoy (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 16:58Z on naval-battles/convoy-r2/screen-cycle-form.md): the escorts at sea with the convoys at once over the convoys at sea at once (station.dd, Q1 (d)); and where 'screen' is read, the escorts on the close screen's stations, the lesser of the escorts with the convoy and the stations, times the radar-fitted share of them, so a thin screen fills fewer stations (Q2 (b)). Stations = 'stations' + the convoy's columns / 'columnsAStation', the columns its ships (count.ships) / 'shipsAColumn': the US Fleet A/S Instructions' screens of 7 to 11 escorts for 3 to 15 columns, 6 + columns / 3 (F, D; historian/escort-screen-cycle-1124.md). shipsAColumn 3.5 (D from L, historian/naval-reads-4-1124.md: HX 229's 37 ships in 11 columns, SC 122's 50 in 14), the columns at most 'maxColumns' 19 (L: HX 300's 166 ships in 19 columns; past that the columns go deeper): the route's 44-ship convoy has 12.6 columns and 10.2 stations (D). No 1940-42 convoy's columns were read, so the rule is D there (the design director, 17:04Z). A null in any of them: the escorts with the convoy are not capped. Escorts beyond the stations add nothing to frustrating attacks (Q3 (a)). While the escorts' losses form is unread they still count in the escort's strength E (Q4 (a)); with it laid they are spare ships that work incidents as coordinated hunts, beside the support groups, and E is the escorts on the stations alone (_escorts, Q2 (a) and Q5). Screens without radar frustrate too: the eye term, laid below; where it is laid it reads only its own figures, and radar alone (t2, rT2) is its fallback. eye (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 17:13Z on naval-battles/convoy-r2/eye-term-form.md, Q1 (a), Q2 and Q3, with the units of 17:24Z and the inputs of 17:17Z): escorts on stations without radar frustrate too, at a lower rate than with it, one rule for every navy: the share that fires = 1 / (1 + c_e e + c_r r), e every escort on the stations for each boat trying (lookouts and asdic), r the radar-fitted ones (a radar-fitted escort counts in both). c_e and c_r are solved together on the record's two points, never on the game. 1941's sample (OEG, Apr-Dec 1941, 17 convoys, F): of 4.2 boats engaging, 2.6 made an effective attack (effective41 0.62, one that torpedoed a ship), a boat that fired putting in n41 4.8 torpedoes (1.7 ships torpedoed x 1.35 hits a ship torpedoed = 2.3 hits, conditional on a hit at 0.45, D), so 0.66 fired; e41 1.07 (4.5 escorts, 'one destroyer and three or four corvettes', F, over 4.2 boats; the reinforced-sample lean of 5-7 is flagged, not laid, e41 1.43 its sensitivity); r41 0.07 (Type 271 about 0 a convoy in April-August and 0.3-1 in September-December 1941, about 0.29 over the period, D on L). T2 (October 1942 to May 1943): 0.3 of attempted attacks not frustrated (F), nT2 5.8 (about 2 torpedoed = 2.7 hits, D), so 0.31 fired; eT2 = rT2 0.97 (about 6.5 escorts, nearly all fitted, over 6.7 boats trying). So c_e about 0.36 and c_r about 1.94 (D); at T2's point the share is 0.31, so the boats that try are the count's pack / 0.31 and the pack comes back there. About three quarters of 1941's convoys were outside 400 nm air reach; the rest is a flagged lean, not fitted out. The check, never fitted: HX 229/SC 122, e and r about 0.5, about 0.46. A null in any eye figure: radar alone, as above.
_load: What a boat that fires puts into one convoy (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 17:27Z on naval-battles/convoy-r2/load-per-convoy-form.md, (a) on all three, with the figures of 17:37Z from historian/finding-b-load-1124.md sections 2.3-2.5 and 3; one rule for every navy, never the date). Torpedoes into one convoy = salvos x the boat's ready tubes (ceiling.tubes), never more than its load: a boat fires all its ready tubes each approach, in both eras (U-100 fired 4 tubes in 5 minutes, U-628 5 in 4, F), and a further approach goes ahead with q = the firing share (the same screen contest, one c pair, Q1 (a): an approach that fails puts the boat down and ends its night) x the share of the night a reload fits in x the share of boats that regain contact after an attack (Q2 (a)). reload 1.25: hours to reload the ready tubes, about 15-20 minutes a tube, 1-1.5 hours for all (D from F: U-100 had 3 tubes ready 35-45 minutes after emptying them, surfaced at night; U-99 reloaded 5 dived in at most 100 minutes); the night's dark hours are the day less its daylight (weather.ts dayShare, the shared astronomy, at the sea's mean latitude), the attack falling at any hour of the dark alike, so a reload fits 1 - reload / dark of the time. regain null (U): contact is lost when running in to attack (F, British 1943-44 summary), and is regained from a shadower's report or the boat's own hydrophone search (F, U-99 by U-101's signal); no share is read, so with it unread a boat that fires makes one approach a convoy, as the record's boats mostly did ('elsewhere a boat got one run per convoy', F; several runs only against a weak screen, HX 72: U-100's six runs, 12 torpedoes). The next night's contact (the boat's surface speed, 17.7-18 knots for a VIIC, against the convoy's 6-8 or 9-13, L; broken by the day's air cover, the sea patrol's keep-down, fitted with it at the one a0 refit, and by a rough sea) waits on the same share. The load is a cap for a patrol, not a convoy (Q3 (a)): a boat holds one load for its days on station (station.ss.patrol), so the torpedoes the route's firing boats put into a month's convoys attacked are never more than its boats on station x their load x 30 / patrol days; past that each convoy's share falls alike. The record's checks, never fitted: about 4.8 torpedoes, 2.3 hits, a boat that fired a convoy in 1941 and 2.7 hits at T2 (the product, ships torpedoed a successful attack x 1.35 hits a ship torpedoed, F/D); escorts attacked 3.2 of 4.2 engaging boats in 1941 (F), and about half of successful attacks went undetected late in 1942 (F); nights in contact 2-5 (F); OEG Table 6 (1941-42), ships sunk a boat in the pack 0.88 at 3.4 escorts, 0.75 at 6.7, 0.34 at 11.1 (F). Null in reload, or tubes null: the whole load into one convoy, as first built. The next night (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 18:00Z, Q2 (a) from its causes; the second run within one night stays unread, 'regain'): a further approach the next night goes ahead with the share of the boats that fired that hold or regain contact through the day, h = the margin of the boat's surface speed over the convoy's (1 - convoy / boat, none where the convoy is as fast: a D form with no figure, flagged), weighed over the route's convoys by class, x the share of its time the aircraft that keep boats down by day leave it up (the sea patrol's keep-down as built, none while the patrol is dormant), x the calm share (a rough sea breaks contact, calmShare as built: D by cause, a VIIC in heavy seas dropping to about the convoy's speed, M; the historian is reading the boats' speed in heavy seas, and if it beats the convoy's, rough months regain through the margin at that speed instead of none). So q = the firing share x (w + (1 - w) x h), w the night's own second run (unread, 0). next.boat 17.85 knots: the VIIC's 17.7-18 on the surface (F, historian/finding-b-load-1124.md; the game builds one boat design, so every boat takes it; the IXC's 18-20 waits on a boat design row). next.convoys: each class's speed and its share of the route's sailings both ways, half each way (the route's convoys sail both ways, count.ways). The Atlantic: slow 7 knots (SC, slow ON and ONS, 6-8, L) and fast 11 knots (HX and fast ON, 9-13, L); eastbound 0.37 slow (D from F: the series' numbering from August 1940, SC 1-177 and HX 59-358), westbound 0.5 slow (D from L/F: the ON convoys alternated fast and slow; the design director, 18:07Z), so 0.185, 0.315, 0.25 and 0.25 of the route's sailings. The spring 1943 change (every ON fast, the slow ships in ONS) is a side's order for its convoys, never a date: on the known list. Libya: 9 knots (L, two convoys, historian/finding-b-load-1124.md section 5), flagged; routing far from a hostile base, which almost doubled the distances, is a staff's choice by the threat: on the known list. _escorts: The escort's incidents and kills by cause (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 17:58Z on naval-battles/convoy-r2/escort-losses-form.md, (a) on Q1 to Q4, with his notes of 17:59Z and 18:00Z, and Q5, 'price once', from his ruling of 16:58Z; and his rulings of 22:24Z on the build's reading, naval-battles/convoy-r2/escort-losses-reading-1124.md: k on the stations solved once on the record's own escorts, 1 (b); the route's seas as built, 2 (a); the support groups shared over the convoys at sea at once, 3 (b); the overshoot named and never tuned, 4 (a)). One rule for every navy; nothing in it reads the date or a nation's flag. The switch: true, laid as shipped (the design director ruled it into the next bundle); null (U), none of it is read and the game is the build before it: the escort meets the count's incidents (0.21 a boat on station a month) at the old split, and E and k stand as the tons ruling set them. Q1 (a): for each convoy attacked, the incidents with the escort are the boats that try x [(1 - f) + f x a]. The screen frustrates 1 - f of them, and finds those that fire with a = 1 - f, the same contest with the same escorts and the same c pair, so no new figure; the incidents are the tries x (1 - f^2). The tries and f are the eye term's (firing.eye: the tries are the count's pack over the eye's share at T2, and f = 1 / (1 + (c_e e + c_r r) / tries), e and r the escorts on the close screen's stations and the radar-fitted ones); with the eye unread they are radar alone's; where no firing share is laid, f = 1, so the screen neither frustrates nor finds after firing and no boat meets the escort. This replaces the count's flat 0.21 for the boats raiding a convoy route, in this build and never before; the 0.21 stays the pack's source (count). A route month's incidents are its convoys attacked x the incidents a convoy attacked, and they fall to its raiding fleets on station by their share of the route's boats on station, as the count's do. a = 1 - f is a one-cause start, flagged. The record's bounds on a by period are checks, never fitted: about 0.125 in 1940, 0.62 or more of the boats that fired attacked in 1941, and about 0.5 of successful attacks detected late in 1942; the game's 1 - f gives about 0.38, 0.34 and 0.69. Named later causes, not built: the escort crews' training and group drill (the one quality store), the air escort inside 1941's figure, and T2's after-firing contest not being independent of the first. The checks at T2, never fitted: the form read about 9.4 incidents a convoy attacked in the game at its 10.3 tries (f about 0.30), and the build's six AI wars give about 8.1 at 8.8 tries (f 0.27, D), against the record's about 6.1 at 6.7 tries (f 0.3); the gap is the boats-on-station gap (the game has about three times the record's boats there), named, never a knob. Boats lost to escorts and support groups by year are set against the record by cause (the historian's: in 1943, 64 of uboat.net's 244 to warships alone and 13 to aircraft and warships together, L, historian/naval-reads-3-1124.md; no page splits close escorts from support groups; 1942, about 86 all causes). In the build's first two wars (D) 1943 has about 147 German and Italian boats lost to all causes, about 135 of them to the Atlantic convoys' escorts, against about 42 (31) with the form unread; 1942 about 100 (87), against about 29 (17). Six AI wars give about 150 (140) in 1943 and 99 (85) in 1942. These kills, and the shares of them below, were read before the 22:24Z rulings, with the support groups counted whole; the reading owed under them reads again the tons by year, the boats lost to escorts by year and by cause, and the months the boat ceiling binds. More than nine in ten of the escort's kills are coordinated (about 0.95 of the expected kills in 1943 and 0.93 in 1942, six wars, D), for the game's escorts with a convoy at T2 are about 35 (33 to 37), the stations' 10.2 filled and about 25 spare, against the record's 6.5 in all: the escorts-a-convoy gap, named, never a knob. The escort's kills in 1943 overshoot the record about twice (about 140 against its 64 to 77). The overshoot is named and never tuned (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 22:24Z, 4 (a)). Its cause is the escorts-a-convoy gap: the game has too few convoys at sea at once, so too many escorts with each. The historian is asked for the North Atlantic's convoys at sea at once by year and the share of escorts at sea, which would close the gap at its cause, the convoy count, and not in this form. The form's Q2 (b), a coordinated hunt taking 2 to 3 ships, stays refused while that figure is U. Q2 (a): an incident is coordinated (OEG Table 10's coordinated column, incident.coordinated with its kit steps) with the chance spare / (spare + on stations), and independent (the independent column) otherwise. Spare is the escorts with a convoy beyond the close screen's stations (firing.screen; they detach to hunt) plus the support groups, its side's destroyers on hunting duty in the route's seas, as the ruling words it: a group hunting in any sea of the route is spare for an incident in any of them, so who works an incident is alike in all the route's seas. The design director accepted this as built at 22:24Z (2 (a)): the hunt's own curve stays in its own sea, so nothing is counted twice. On stations is the escorts filling the close screen. Each ship works at its own navy's column and kit steps and its readiness. No new figure. The split is for one convoy (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 22:24Z, 3 (b)). The escorts beyond the stations sail with the convoy, so they are counted a convoy, as the screen counts them. A support group or a hunting-duty ship is in one place at a time, so its ships are shared over the route's convoys at sea at once: each convoy's spare is its escorts beyond the stations plus the groups' ships over the convoys at sea at once. Counted whole with each convoy, one ship would be priced several times over. The convoys at sea at once are the count the screen already shares the escorts over (station.dd): the convoys sailed a month x a convoy's crossing over the month's 30 days, about 3.3 on the Atlantic route at T2 (D); while the escorts' cycle is unread, the convoys sailed a month, as the screen first counted. No new figure. Where fewer than one convoy is at sea at once, a group is whole with the one, never more: the one-place-at-a-time rule, a group's share is its ships over the larger of 1 and the convoys at sea, so no ship counts twice (kept by the design director, 24 November 2026 23:57Z, 3). With no convoy sailed, the groups add nothing. That rule binds on no route the game ships: the convoys at sea at once are set by figures the game never changes (the route's tons, the ways, its convoy's ships and their GRT, and the crossing), about 3.3 on the Atlantic route and 10 on the Libya route (D), so keeping it or removing it changes nothing in play. The escorts and the groups are both counted for one convoy, but not alike over time. An escort bound to the route counts at the escorts' cycle's share at sea (station.dd: 19 of 33 days with a convoy, times 1 - 0.333 in service, about 0.384, D), over the convoys at sea at once; with the cycle unread, the two are alike over the convoys sailed. A group's ships carry no such share: the game counts a fleet on hunting duty at sea in full, as the hunt's curve does (fleets.json hunt.hunter 1), and the ruling shares a group over the convoys at sea at once and names no share at sea for it, so none is laid. So for one convoy a destroyer on hunting duty in the route's seas counts about 2.85 times one bound to the route's escort: 1 in the coordinated column and 0.25 x 0.384 = 0.096 more through the screen's loose share (below), against 0.384, each over the convoys at sea at once (D). Where the close screen's stations are not full, the convoys at sea at once cancel from spare / (spare + on stations), and that ratio alone sets the coordinated share. This is built as ruled, named and never tuned. In the grand campaign a group hunting in one of the route's seas also counts at the loose share (fleets.json escort.loose, 0.25) among the escorts with each convoy, as the screen and the route's escort worth have always counted it. That count is unchanged, but the group's own part is now shared over the convoys at sea, so the overlap is about a tenth of that part (0.096 against 1, D), where with the groups counted whole it was about 3% on the Atlantic route (0.096 / 3.3, D). The overlap is named and left as built. Q3 (a): escort ships sunk keep the flat escortLoss (navy.json convoy) until the fleet actions' form (#6). Q4 (a): boats not raiding keep the hunt's curve exactly as before (fleets.json hunt, the hunt's 1 - raiding split), and only the raiding boats' incidents change. The hunt's ships never take a raiding boat on the curve as well, so a support group that works its incidents does not hunt it twice: nothing is counted twice. Q5, price once: with the extras hunting, the contest's escort strength E is the escorts on the close screen's stations with the convoy, a count of ships, and k is solved once on it at the tons ruling's own record point, on the record's own E there, 6.5 escorts a convoy (count.sinkOnStations 0.984; the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 22:24Z, 1 (b); the arithmetic is in _count). Where the form is laid it replaces the tons ruling's 0.137, which was solved on the game's escort worth a convoy with the same inflation. The game's E on the stations at T2 is 10.19, high because the game has too few convoys at sea and so too many escorts with each, a fault named and never tuned. So at T2 the contest gives about 3.05 ships a convoy attacked, under the boat ceiling's about 3.15 and under T2's 3.2 to 4.4, and the 1943 Atlantic tons fall about 8.0% (3.7% to 13.6%) against k unread in six AI wars with the groups shared (D): the fault's honest effect, shown and not tuned. Solved on the game's 10.19, k would be 0.628 and the ceiling would decide every month to the end of 1943; that was refused, for it would bake the fault into the constant and need a second refit once the convoy count is mended. The ships on the stations are the ones the screen already reads, so away from T2 a bigger screen both lets fewer boats fire and cuts what each sinks, where the record has about two ships torpedoed in each attack that succeeded whatever the screen (OEG 51 section 5.2.1, F): E on the stations prices again what the screen and the incidents price. Built as ruled, and noted.
_patrol: The sea patrol against submarines (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 15:14Z on naval-battles/convoy-r2/sea-patrol-form.md, (a) on all nine questions, with his marks of 15:14Z, 15:23Z and 15:32Z). A land bomber group on the standing order 'Patrol the [sea] against submarines' watches a share of that sea: s = R x (1 - e^(-A / A_R)), R the share of the sea's waters it reaches, A the aircraft on patrol there (each group's bombers x its readiness x the sky, none from a grounded field or under a closed sky, half under cloud, at the air rules' cover curve over its distance: full to 0.6 of its range, half at its limit), A_R the aircraft that watch the waters reached. 'reach' says how R and A_R are read: 'map', as the design director ruled for the dormant interim (his ruling of 24 November 2026 17:49Z, 4), R the share of the sea's squares on the chart within the group's bomber range of its airfield and A_R = a0 for each 10,000 square nautical miles of them, to be replaced at the one a0 refit by the aircraft type's radius on the map geometry; 'air', as first ruled at 15:14Z and no longer the reading, R the sea's 'air' share and A_R = a0 x R / air. A sea is reached at all as a strike is judged (its nearest coast within bomber range), all of it with long-range patrol aircraft. intensity: the air fighting's own row where enemy fighters meet a patrol, as they meet a strike over the sea (air.ts assessAir; the air thread's Q6), U until laid. It gates only the fighters (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 17:49Z, 5 (a)): while it is unread no enemy fighter meets a patrol and none of its bombers is lost to them, and the patrol itself works. A patrol loses only the fighters' part of what a strike there would lose, since an open sea has no guns, and nothing to the enemy where no fighter comes up (seapatrol.ts patrolLoss); its losses are booked to the group's and the nation's, as a raid's are. The computer's staff sends only bomber groups with no fighters: a patrol flies alone, and a bomber group defends nothing. It sends them where its side last saw boats, never where they truly are, and predicts no move of theirs. It weighs a group's patrol against the raid its raid staff chose for the group, at that raid's own score, before the raid flies, and a group the raid staff left on support against nothing; the patrol goes wherever it is worth more, with no other test (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 17:49Z, 2 (a) and 3 (a)). A computer-run raider's staff moves its beat out of waters where its side's boats last met aircraft without kit, never reading the patrols truly flown, and only where the month's gain in time up on station, each beat read from the port the staff would base it at, is more than the move itself loses: for its boats on station, the passage from the old beat to the new (station.ss.passage days a sea crossed, by the sea graph), or the whole month in harbour where the move takes it to another base and keeping its beat would not; and where keeping its beat would take it to another base and the move would not, the month in harbour that staying costs counts for the move (17:49Z, 1 (a)). a0: fitted through the game to the historian's arc of sinkings inside shore reach, 1940 to October 1941 (historian/air-vs-subs-1124.md section 8), at each quarter's anti-submarine hours, never standalone (U until fitted). In watched waters a boat on station is attacked 'attacks' times a month, by the kit its attackers carry (depth charges and sea-search radar: convoycause.json 'asv'), and 'kill' of those attacks sink it (U until read: the historian's 2.5% of attacks in 1941 to 25% in 1943-44 are by date and wait to be set against kit). The boats sunk are booked inside the hunt's cap, on their own dice. Aircraft without the kit keep the boats down instead: a boat's time on station in the waters they watch counts at 1 - s for finding and attacking convoys and meeting the escort; with the kit, OEG T7's cut ('cover') stands at the share watched, and Q4's kills with it, no keeping down on top. Each staff counts the other side's units where its own side last saw them (the design director's 24 November 2026 17:49Z amendment to ruling 1, and his ruling of 17:54Z on naval-battles/convoy-r2/sight-store-form.md, (a) on all five questions): while the patrol is live, each nation keeps one record a sea (seasight.ts) of the enemy boats it last saw there (its convoys attacked, its escort met, its patrols sighted, it sank, or its search identified them, the most any one of these showed; a fleet only reported is not counted, as the map counts no strength for it) and of the enemy aircraft its own boats last met there (the watch each enemy patrol kept over its boats as the patrol's own month booked it, so a patrol is seen once it has flown over the boats, never at its order), each with its month, written at the close of its month at sea and read by its staffs and its allies' and by the player's own panel; a sea never seen counts as clear, there is no decay figure, and nothing is written or read while the patrol is dormant. 'lost': the share of the aircraft on patrol lost a month (U: about 2 aircraft a 1,000 hours flown, D, waits for the hours an aircraft flies a month). 'live': the switch (the design director's ruling of 24 November 2026 17:49Z, 5 (a)): the patrol runs only when live is true and a0, attacks and kill are laid. It is false as shipped, so the patrol is dormant until the one a0 refit, and going live needs Brian's card; if intensity is still null then, that is the open gap, and no enemy fighter meets a patrol until the air thread's row is laid. While live is false, or a0, attacks or kill are unread (null), nothing here is read: no order is offered, and the flat air term in the hunt and the cover from coasts held stand (the design director's mark: never remove a working cause before its replacement is laid). Laid as interim (the design director's rulings of 24 November 2026 16:58Z, 17:06Z, 17:10Z and 17:13Z on naval-battles/convoy-r2/sea-patrol-a0-reading-1124.md), the patrol still dormant while live is false: a0 8 aircraft on patrol to each 10,000 square nautical miles reached (D, read through the game on the fall of the historian's section 8 arc, 4 seeds; one refit owed once daylight, the ships' density near the home ports and the route's western seas are laid, on the arc re-cut to the game's water and bases, historian/naval-reads-4-1124.md section 3). attacks: none 2.65 a boat-month watched (D from F: 8 attacks a month, Jul 1940-Mar 1941, over about 5 boats on station x 0.60 of them inside reach, the section 8 arc's mean for those quarters); kit 2.92, radar finding 1.1 times as often by day (D, OEG ch. 13 Table 2, F: ESF and Trinidad straddle 1) and nothing more by night without a searchlight; 18 and 39 a month in 1941 are checks, never fitted. kill 0.025 of attacks for every air force (F, 1941); radar adds no kill until the share of attacks catching a boat surfaced is laid (warning receivers, depth settings and fill, the searchlight: rows the tree lacks; 0.10 of 1942-43 is a check, never laid). lost 0.04 of the aircraft on patrol a month to weather and accident (D on L: about half of 2 a 1,000 hours, 116 of 233 to May 1943, x 40 hours a month), flat until the game's own flying weather by season is tied in; enemy losses only through intensity, so nothing counts twice. By day only: the boats are kept down, and the kit's cut acts, for the day's share of their time, the sun's day over the sea's mean latitude that month (weather.ts dayShare, astronomy, F; 17:10Z); about 0.7 of convoy attacks at night, Jul 1940-Mar 1941 (F), is the check.
